theorem: Let O_src and O_lean be the two detector subsets of the unit flat 3-torus defined by the exact source and Lean coordinate inequalities. There is no normalized-Haar-measure-preserving bijection F:T^3->T^3 such that F(O_src)=O_lean, since mu(O_src)=3/32 and mu(O_lean)=1/2. In particular no volume-preserving smooth torus diffeomorphism or rigid torus isometry identifies these entire detector sets.
proof: Each detector is the product of an open interval in one unit-circle coordinate with two unrestricted unit-circle factors. Thus normalized Haar measure equals interval length: 1/8-1/32=3/32 for the October source, and 1-1/2=1/2 for the Lean adjacent theorem. A measure-preserving bijection satisfies mu(F(O_src))=mu(O_src), contradicting 3/32 != 1/2 if F(O_src)=O_lean. The coordinate-index difference does not affect the volume computation. Endpoints have measure zero.
positive_controls: Both statements are fixed-particle halting detectors on spatially unit-periodic three-dimensional geometries, with concrete initial labels and open detector slabs.
A spatial translation can match the initial points alone; this does not identify the detector sets.
hostile_controls: Reject the claim that equal halting truth values imply equal detector sets or conjugate velocity fields.
Reject the claim that this excludes arbitrary non-volume-preserving diffeomorphisms or event equivalence under different observation predicates.
Reject the claim that the October manuscript is refuted, that the Lean theorem is false, or that the two constructions must be identical.
